model.architecture: Compact vision-language model: SigLIP vision encoder (384x384) + MLP projector + Qwen2-0.5B decoder, LiteRT-LM fast_vlm bundle

variants.quantization: decoder int4 (symmetric, blockwise-32 + OCTAV); SigLIP vision encoder + MLP projector int8; tied embedding INT8 (externalized)

recommended.reason: measured on one Galaxy S26 with one binary: GPU 83.88 tok/s decode / 1233.4 prefill, peak 441 MB, init 1.3 s (S4 GPU gate 2026-08-25, 1 run) against CPU 69.64 decode / 301.9 prefill, peak 603 MB, init 0.9 s (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-05, 2 cold runs). Same-device CPU control taken - a measured win for gpu on decode (1.2x) and prefill

platform_notes: Context (KV cache) 2048; image input resized to 384x384
iPhone/macOS (Swift runtime / LiteRTDemo): load with the vision tower enabled (Modality.textImage / [.vision]); vision-only bundle, no audio tower
Android: Google AI Edge Gallery import must check 'Support image' (required for image input); pick GPU (fast) or CPU; v1.0.16+ imports directly from Hugging Face
Best for single-image VQA: ask about one image per chat and start a new conversation for a different image

measured.source: S4 GPU gate, 205-token benchmark, single run; full delegation (3098 ops across 3 subgraphs); generation gate answered the probe correctly. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is a GPU speed, not a measured win over CPU.

S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); the GPU path does not run for this file on this handset, so this row has no GPU counterpart

known_issues: Becomes unreliable when a second image is added to the same conversation (the answer truncates) — single-image VQA only, new conversation per image
